title: f120.3: PeerHealthState — per-peer health tracking with round-robin selection
description:
Implement PeerHealthState for tracking per-relay health and selecting peers for delivery.

**What:** Arc<Mutex<>> struct tracking up/down state, timestamps, and round-robin selection across healthy peers.

**Algorithm:**
1. Create crates/smtp/src/relay_health.rs
2. Define struct PeerStatus { host_port: String, is_up: bool, last_success: Option<Instant>, last_failure: Option<Instant>, attempt_count: u64, success_count: u64, failure_count: u64 }
3. Define struct PeerHealthState { peers: Vec<PeerStatus>, rr_index: usize, down_backoff: Duration }
4. impl PeerHealthState:
   - fn new(hosts: &[SmtpRelayPeerConfig], down_backoff: Duration) -> Self
   - fn mark_up(&mut self, idx: usize) — set is_up=true, last_success=Instant::now(), increment success_count
   - fn mark_down(&mut self, idx: usize) — set is_up=false, last_failure=Instant::now(), increment failure_count
   - fn record_attempt(&mut self, idx: usize) — increment attempt_count
   - fn select_peer(&mut self) -> Option<(usize, &SmtpRelayPeerConfig)> — returns (index, config) of next peer to try:
     a. Build candidate list: peers where is_up=true, OR where last_failure is None, OR where last_failure.elapsed() > down_backoff
     b. Round-robin across candidates: advance rr_index, wrap modulo candidate count
     c. Return None if no candidates at all
   - fn all_peers(&self) -> &[PeerStatus] — for metrics export

**Defensive programming rules:**
- Never unwrap() on the mutex lock (poison = bugs in other code; propagate via expect with context)
- select_peer() must never return the same peer twice in a row if other up peers exist (round-robin correctness)
- All timestamps use std::time::Instant (monotonic; never system time for backoff decisions)

**Tests:**
- Test: single peer, starts up, select_peer() returns it (oracle: expected index 0)
- Test: single peer, mark_down(), select_peer() returns None within down_backoff window (oracle: manually advance time? — use tokio::time::pause/advance in test)  
- Test: two peers, mark first down, select_peer() returns second peer only
- Test: two peers both up, multiple select_peer() calls alternate between them (round-robin correctness)
- Test: peer marked down then select_peer() called after backoff elapsed returns it again

**Acceptance:**
- cargo test -p usenet-ipfs-smtp passes
- cargo clippy -p usenet-ipfs-smtp -- -D warnings passes
- Round-robin test demonstrates no sticky-peer behavior
